name: WI-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+26 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Incumbent Gwen Moore running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger Tim Rogers has reported no fundraising
Prediction markets price Moore at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: This Milwaukee-area seat leans Democratic by 26 points, Moore is a well-established incumbent, and her challenger has shown no measurable fundraising or outside support. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Moore win, so the forecast stays at the baseline margin.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing a competitive race or a major outside-spending intervention for Rogers would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gwen Moore has held this Milwaukee-based House seat since 2005, and the district's partisan lean of roughly 26 points Democratic makes it one of the safest Democratic seats in Wisconsin. Moore enters the general election with over $1 million raised, though limited cash on hand, while Republican Tim Rogers has reported no fundraising activity and no outside groups are spending in the race.

Prediction markets give Moore about a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the contest as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's strong Democratic fundamentals, Moore's incumbency advantage, and her clear financial edge, all pointing to a comfortable double-digit victory.
